subject.title: Add structured process events for sessions

question: Should OpenClaw core define a new session-level `process.*` / `step.*` event contract now, and what taxonomy, replay, authorization, and redaction model should own it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the solution creates a public core event contract and exposes intermediate run state, so automation should not choose the product and security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Core Contract First
options.body: Keep the issue open for a maintainer-owned design that defines taxonomy, observer permissions, replay/retention, redaction, and mappings from existing event streams before implementation.

options.title: Scope To Existing Streams
options.body: Narrow the request to better document and extend current `agent`, `item`, `plan`, and `session.tool` events without creating new `process.*` / `step.*` names.

options.title: Defer Process Events
options.body: Leave existing progress surfaces as-is and close only after maintainers explicitly decide that structured process events are not part of the near-term core roadmap.

recommendation.title: Design Core Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open for a maintainer-owned design that defines taxonomy, observer permissions, replay/retention, redaction, and mappings from existing event streams before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the clearest adjacent feature-history signal for item lifecycle events and gateway protocol documentation, and this choice is primarily a core product/API direction call.
